concerns.text: A normal 37 degrees Celsius rectal temperature in a 21-day-old newborn who felt subjectively warm to the touch tonight supports unbundling and home observation (level 1), though some pediatricians advise an outpatient clinic check or nurse triage review whenever a neonate under 28 days is reported as feeling warm (level 2).

Fatigue after missing 6 days of thrice-weekly hemodialysis warrants immediate hospital serum potassium and electrocardiogram screening with emergent dialysis (level 4), though when cardiopulmonary red flags are absent some nephrology teams arrange an urgent same-day add-on session at the patient's outpatient dialysis center (level 3).

Three weeks of postmenopausal vaginal blood spotting 6 years after menopause requires transvaginal ultrasound and endometrial assessment via an outpatient gynecologist (level 3), though in primary-care-first systems initial pelvic examination and fast-track ultrasound ordering by a general practitioner is also standard (level 2).

Recurrent dark red gross hematuria with small blood clots in a 64-year-old former dye-factory worker requires urology specialist cystoscopy and CT urography (level 3), though in gatekeeper systems initial urgent primary-care urinalysis, renal function check, and fast-track urology referral is also standard (level 2).

Six weeks of fatigable evening bilateral ptosis and diplopia fits outpatient neurology or neuro-ophthalmology specialist evaluation for ocular myasthenia gravis (level 3), though when new binocular diplopia with ptosis has not yet undergone neuroimaging or bulbar screening some clinicians recommend urgent emergency assessment first (level 4).

Deep cat-tooth puncture wounds on the dorsum of the hand with early mild local redness at 8 hours are managed at a same-day outpatient clinic with wound irrigation and oral amoxicillin-clavulanate (level 2), though given the risk of rapid Pasteurella deep-space hand infection some clinicians route deep cat bites on the hand directly to the emergency department (level 4).

Six days of unilateral foul-smelling purulent nasal discharge in a 3-year-old toddler warrants prompt outpatient clinic anterior rhinoscopy for suspected nasal foreign body (level 2), though practices without pediatric suction or extraction instruments commonly refer directly to otolaryngology or emergency removal (level 3).
